security_audit.summary: All 154 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown links, code formatting, redacted placeholders, and documented calls to expected endpoints. No prompt injection, hidden execution, unrelated destination, or real embedded secret was found. Paid third-party requests and automatic x402 settlement still create a spending risk that users should control.

remediation.issue: Paid requests can settle before data delivery.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation for top-ups and x402 payments. Add spending caps, call limits, and cost estimates before repeated requests.

content.value_statement: Official TikTok access can require application review and does not fit quick, read-only research. This skill guides paid Fetcher.sh requests for posts, profiles, comments, and discovery feeds.
actual_capabilities: Searches TikTok posts by keyword with supported sorting, date, region, and cursor parameters.
Looks up a post by share URL or numeric ID.
Retrieves profiles, user posts, followers, and following lists through documented endpoints.
Retrieves comments, replies, hashtag posts, sound posts, and location posts.
Provides REST, curl, OpenAPI, and MCP usage guidance.
Supports prepaid Bearer credentials or per-call x402 payments.
limitations: Every data request costs $0.004, and upstream failures are not refunded.
Results depend on Fetcher.sh and TikTok availability, latency, and returned fields.
No webhook, streaming, posting, liked-post, or server-side CSV export capability is provided.
Users must evaluate TikTok terms, privacy obligations, and regional rules for their use case.

use_cases.title: Track content trends
use_cases.description: Search recent or most-liked posts for selected keywords and compare recurring topics.

use_cases.title: Research creator audiences
use_cases.description: Resolve creator profiles, review their posts, and paginate follower or following lists.

use_cases.title: Build a research pipeline
use_cases.description: Collect paginated post, hashtag, sound, location, and comment data for downstream analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find recent posts
prompt_templates.prompt: Search TikTok for posts about [keyword] from [date range]. Return the most recent results with creator, date, engagement, and link.

prompt_templates.title: Review a creator
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up TikTok creator [handle]. Summarize the profile and recent posts, then identify recurring themes and engagement patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor a hashtag
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve hashtag [name], collect its posts across available pages, and summarize new post IDs, creators, themes, and engagement since [date].

prompt_templates.title: Design a controlled pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a paginated TikTok collection for [research goal]. Include endpoints, cursor handling, deduplication, regional scope, cost limits, retries, and privacy controls.

output_examples.input: Find the most-liked AI agent posts from this month.
output: A ranked summary of matching posts with creator names, engagement totals, publication dates, and links.
A short synthesis of repeated topics and notable outliers.

output_examples.input: Review the profile and recent posts for a specified creator.
output_examples.output: A profile overview followed by recent post themes, engagement observations, and the identifiers needed for deeper queries.

output_examples.input: Create a weekly hashtag monitoring workflow with a $2 budget.
output_examples.output: A bounded polling plan with endpoint order, cursor storage, deduplication rules, cost estimates, and a concise weekly report format.

best_practices: Confirm the expected call count and budget before pagination or scheduled polling.
Keep the Bearer key in a protected environment variable and redact it from logs.
Store cursors and post IDs so repeated runs can resume and avoid duplicate paid calls.
anti_patterns: Do not expose Bearer credentials in prompts, reports, source control, or shared logs.
Do not run unbounded polling or pagination without explicit cost and stop limits.
Do not treat returned fields, availability, or platform compliance as guaranteed.

faq.question: Do I need a TikTok developer account?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses the separate Fetcher.sh service, which does not require TikTok application review.

faq.question: How is each request authenticated?
faq.answer: Use a prepaid Fetcher.sh Bearer key or an x402 payment supported by the service.

faq.question: How much does a data request cost?
faq.answer: The documentation states a flat price of $0.004 for each endpoint call.

faq.question: Can searches use dates, sorting, and regions?
faq.answer: Keyword search supports documented sort and date values. Region is available on selected endpoints.

faq.question: How are additional result pages retrieved?
faq.answer: Pass the returned cursor to the next request until the service stops returning another cursor.

faq.question: Can this skill post videos or export CSV files?
faq.answer: No. It provides read-only data access, and CSV export must be implemented by the caller.
